Answer: D
Reason: The chest radiograph shows right-sided volume loss with mediastinal shift to the right and a characteristic "kinked" or anomalous vessel in the right cardiophrenic angle, which are classic signs of right upper lobe hypoplasia (often associated with scimitar syndrome variants) where the remaining right lung lobes undergo compensatory hyperaeration. This distinguishes it from agenesis (which would show complete absence of lung tissue/vasculature) or simple atelectasis.
